{{ElectionsMT}}
The '''2026 United States Senate election in Montana''' will be held on November 3, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Montana]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] U.S. Attorney [[Kurt Alme]], [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Air Force officer Alani Bankhead, and [[Independent politician|independent]] former [[University of Montana]] president [[Seth Bodnar]] are the major candidates. Republican incumbent [[Steve Daines]] is not seeking a third term.

Bodnar, supported by former Democratic senator [[Jon Tester]], launched an independent campaign on March 4, 2026 shortly after resigning from the University of Montana.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Federal Elections Commission |first1=United States |title=Seth Bodnar Filing |url=https://www.fec.gov/data/committee/C00941708/ |website=Seth Bodnar Filing March 4 |publisher=FEC |access-date=29 May 2026}}</ref> Primaries were held on June 2. In the Republican primary, Daines announced he would seek re-election, but withdrew minutes before the filing deadline and endorsed Alme, who filed to run the same day. As the only major Republican candidate, Alme was nominated with 76.2% of the vote. Bankhead won the Democratic nomination with 43.7% of the vote over former state representative [[Reilly Neill]] and tribal historic preservation officer Michael Black Wolf.

== Background ==
This is the first open Senate election in Montana since [[1976 United States Senate election in Montana|1976]].{{cn|date=October 2026}}

Montana is considered to be a red state at the federal level, having not voted for a Democratic president since [[Bill Clinton]]'s [[1992 United States presidential election in Montana|plurality victory in 1992]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.270towin.com/states/montana|title=Montana Presidential Election Voting History - 270toWin|website=270toWin.com}}</ref> Recently, the state has also been trending red on a statewide level, as Republicans flipped the governorship in [[2020 Montana gubernatorial election|2020]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vox.com/2020/11/4/21536492/election-results-greg-gianforte-montana-governor-winner|title=Greg Gianforte flips Montana governorship to Republicans|first=Benjamin|last=Rosenberg|date=November 4, 2020|website=Vox}}</ref> and the Class I Senate seat in [[2024 United States Senate election in Montana|2024]].<ref>https://www.npr.org/2024/11/09/nx-s1-5181908/with-democratic-senator-jon-testers-loss-in-montana-republicans-take-full-control</ref>

== Republican primary ==
The filing deadline for participation in primaries was March 5, 2026, at 5:00 p.m.<ref>{{Cite web |title = 2026 PRIMARY AND GENERAL ELECTION CALENDAR |publisher = Montana Secretary of State  |date  = October 2025 |url = https://sosmt.gov/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?juwpfisadmin=false&action=wpfd&task=file.download&wpfd_category_id=27&wpfd_file_id=72177&token=6f7af6195f33954ee91f868f73055133&preview=1}}</ref> At 4:52 p.m. [[Kurt Alme]] filed to run, and 3 minutes later [[Steve Daines]] withdrew. At 5:02 p.m. Daines announced his withdrawal and endorsed Alme. The last minute switch was seen as controversial.<ref>{{Cite news|last = Browning |first = Kellen |title = A Sly Political Switcheroo Stuns Montana and Starts a New Senate Fight |publisher = The New York Times |date = March 5, 2026 |url = https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/05/us/politics/steve-daines-montana-senate-alme.html}}</ref> Daines's maneuver has been criticized by members of both parties.<ref name="auto">{{cite web |last1=Weaver |first1=Al |last2=Brooks |first2=Emily |title=Daines’s last-minute retirement maneuver leaves Capitol Hill stunned — and some frustrated |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/5772231-steve-daines-retirement-maneuver/ |publisher=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]] |access-date=September 8, 2026 |date=March 7, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/03/04/politics/steve-daines-kurt-alme-trump|title=Montana GOP Sen. Steve Daines won’t seek reelection in shock announcement at filing deadline &#124; CNN Politics|first=Lauren Fox, Ethan|last=Cohen|date=March 5, 2026|website=[[CNN]]}}</ref> After the announcement, the [[Montana Republican Party]] announced they would not endorse any candidates in any federal races, saying it "supports a competitive primary process to let voters pick their preferred candidates."<ref name="gopend">{{cite web |title=Montana GOP won’t endorse in federal races this cycle |url=https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/montana-gop-wont-endorse-federal-races-cycle |website=News From The States |access-date=6 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

== Democratic primary ==
Five candidates stood in the Democratic primary. By the end of March, the Democratic field had collectively raised $123,629.43, the vast majority of which was by Reilly Neill, a former state legislator. Neill launched her campaign for Senate immediately following [[Jon Tester]]'s loss to [[Tim Sheehy]] in [[2024 United States Senate election in Montana|2024]], and had run a [[write-in]] campaign in [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Montana|2024]] for the [[Montana's 2nd congressional district|second district]] to the U.S. house, after John Driscoll, the Democratic candidate, refused to spend more than $5,000 on his campaign.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lutey |first1=Tom |title=In Senate race, underfunded Democrats try to fend off a challenge from the middle |url=https://montanafreepress.org/2026/05/08/in-senate-race-underfunded-democrats-try-to-fend-off-a-challenge/ |access-date=June 4, 2026 |work=[[Montana Free Press]] |date=May 8, 2026 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/VsvPj |archive-date=June 4, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> A poll conducted in late April and early May for the ''[[Montana Free Press]]'' by [[Eagleton Institute of Politics|Eagleton]] suggested that the Democratic candidates for Senate were largely unknown by Montanans.<ref name="Lutey-2026">{{cite news |last1=Lutey |first1=Tom |title=Montana U.S. Senate candidates largely unknown to voters, poll finds |url=https://montanafreepress.org/2026/05/19/montana-us-senate-candidates-largely-unknown-to-voters/ |access-date=June 4, 2026 |work=[[Montana Free Press]] |date=May 19, 2026 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/nWF5q |archive-date=June 4, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Alani Bankhead, an Air Force veteran based in [[Helena, Montana|Helena]], had raised just over $10,000 by the end of March, leaving her at a heavy financial disadvantage. However, in May, the Progressive Vet PAC ([[political action committee]]) spent $592,000 on mailers in support of Bankhead.<ref name="Lutey-2026a">{{cite news |last1=Lutey |first1=Tom |title=The mailers fueling speculation in Montana’s Democratic primary for U.S. Senate |url=https://montanafreepress.org/2026/05/15/the-mailers-fueling-speculation-in-montanas-democratic-primary-for-u-s-senate/ |access-date=4 June 2026 |work=[[Montana Free Press]] |date=15 May 2026 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/CjeSf |archive-date=4 June 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Meanwhile, the More Jobs, Less Government PAC invested in ads attacking Neill as a liberal, and saying that Bankhead would work with [[Donald Trump]].<ref name="Lutey-2026b">{{cite news |last1=Lutey |first1=Tom |title=The Sheehy-supporting PAC trying to define Montana’s Democratic Senate candidates |url=https://montanafreepress.org/2026/05/26/the-sheehy-supporting-pac-trying-to-define-montanas-democratic-senate-candidates/ |access-date=4 June 2026 |work=[[Montana Free Press]] |date=26 May 2026 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/MT1Lj |archive-date=4 June 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Everett-2026">{{cite news |last1=Everett |first1=Burgess |title=Why groups are spending big in Montana’s Democratic Senate primary |url=https://www.semafor.com/article/06/01/2026/why-groups-are-spending-big-in-montanas-democratic-senate-primary |access-date=4 June 2026 |work=[[Semafor (website)|Semafor]] |date=1 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260604075713/https://www.semafor.com/article/06/01/2026/why-groups-are-spending-big-in-montanas-democratic-senate-primary |archive-date=4 June 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> The Progressive Vet PAC, founded in April 2026, had former Democratic state representative [[Moffie Funk]] as its treasurer, while the More Jobs, Less Government PAC worked to promote the election of Sheehy, a Republican, in 2024. Financial filings by the More Jobs, Less Government PAC declared that their ads were in support of Bankhead, although the Progressive Vet PAC has said that the attack ads are designed to elevate Neill over Bankhead.<ref name="Lutey-2026a" /><ref name="Lutey-2026b" />

Brian Miller, a candidate for the U.S. House in the second district, suggested that Progressive Vet's spending was designed to benefit independent candidate [[Seth Bodnar]], in the hopes Bankhead would win the primary and drop out in support of Bodnar. Neill publicly stated she would not drop out of the general election, and when asked by the ''Montana Free Press'' if she would drop out, Bankhead said "not only no, but hell no".<ref name="Lutey-2026a" />

Both Neill and Bankhead campaigned in rural areas of Montana. Neill supported expansion of the [[Family Medical Leave Act]], new educational grants, and rural healthcare, while Bankhead advocated for cuts to [[red tape]], greater accountability in government, and protecting children and the elderly.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hansen |first1=Jordan |title=Neill, Bankhead look to court rural voters in Senate primary |url=https://dailymontanan.com/2026/05/28/neill-bankhead-look-to-court-rural-voters-in-senate-primary/ |access-date=June 4, 2026 |work=Daily Montanan |date=May 28, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260604075640/https://dailymontanan.com/2026/05/28/neill-bankhead-look-to-court-rural-voters-in-senate-primary/ |archive-date=June 4, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The [[Associated Press]] called the primary for Bankhead at 9:53pm on election night. Preliminary figures showed Bankhead with 44% of the vote to Neill's 33%. Michael Black Wolf, a [[tribal historic preservation officer]] from the [[Fort Belknap Indian Community]], placed third with 13%.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hansen |first1=Jordan |title=Bankhead wins Dem Senate primary |url=https://dailymontanan.com/2026/06/02/bankhead-holds-early-lead-over-neill-in-dem-primary/ |access-date=June 2, 2026 |work=Daily Montana |date=June 4, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260604090556/https://dailymontanan.com/2026/06/02/bankhead-holds-early-lead-over-neill-in-dem-primary/ |archive-date=June 4, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Lutey |first1=Tom |title=Republican Kurt Alme and Democrat Alani Bankhead declared Senate primary winners by The Associated Press |url=https://montanafreepress.org/2026/06/02/kurt-alme-wins-republican-primary-for-senate/ |access-date=June 4, 2026 |work=[[Montana Free Press]] |date=June 2, 2026 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/3X0D1 |archive-date=June 4, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Speaking to [[KTVH]] about the results of the primary, Jeremy Johnson, a professor from [[Carroll College]] who chairs their Department of Political Science and International Relations, said that Republicans were likely to prefer running against both a Democrat and independent, and "if that could be consolidated down to one candidate, it'd be interesting to see what that could look like in November".<ref name="Ambarian-2026">{{cite news |last1=Ambarian |first1=Jonathon |title=Political science professor reacts to Montana primary results |url=https://www.ktvh.com/news/montana-politics/political-science-professor-reacts-to-montana-primary-results |access-date=June 4, 2026 |work=[[KTVH]] |date=June 3, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260604090529/https://www.ktvh.com/news/montana-politics/political-science-professor-reacts-to-montana-primary-results |archive-date=June 4, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Libertarian primary ==
The Libertarian primary was contested by two candidates — [[Clancy, Montana|Clancy]] resident Tom Jandron, and Billings pharmacist Kyle Austin, twice a candidate in the Republican U.S. House primary for the 2nd district.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lutey |first1=Tom |title=Is Montana having a Libertarian moment? |url=https://montanafreepress.org/2026/03/18/is-montana-having-a-libertarian-moment/ |access-date=June 4, 2026 |work=[[Montana Free Press]] |date=March 18, 2026 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/Vjb2g |archive-date=June 4, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Jandron was unanimously endorsed by Libertarian delegates for Senate at the party's April convention, with the party stating that he was more ideologically aligned to libertarian ideals than Austin.<ref name="Lepeska-2026">{{cite news |last1=Lepeska |first1=David |title=Libertarians back Clancy’s Jandron for U.S. Senate |url=https://jcmonitor.com/libertarians-back-clancys-jandron-for-u-s-senate/ |access-date=June 4, 2026 |work=[[The Boulder Monitor|The Monitor]] |date=April 29, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260604093536/https://jcmonitor.com/libertarians-back-clancys-jandron-for-u-s-senate/ |archive-date=June 4, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Austin opposed increasing the size of the federal government and the national debt. He expressed concern about changes by Congress in 2025 to limit access to [[Medicaid]], but supported work requirements for benefits. Jandron supported the [[Defend the Guard]] proposal, said that Republicans in Montana had not done enough to counter rising spending or government surveillance, and described himself as an ideological libertarian, having been a member of the party for five years.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ambarian |first1=Jonathon |title=Primary 2026: Two Libertarian candidates seek chance to provide alternative in U.S. Senate race |url=https://www.ktvh.com/news/montana-politics/primary-2026-two-libertarian-candidates-seek-chance-to-provide-alternative-in-u-s-senate-race |access-date=June 4, 2026 |work=[[KTVH]] |date=May 7, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260604093734/https://www.ktvh.com/news/montana-politics/primary-2026-two-libertarian-candidates-seek-chance-to-provide-alternative-in-u-s-senate-race |archive-date=June 4, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Austin won the primary, but was disavowed by the Montana Libertarian Party.<ref name="Ambarian-2026"/>

== Independent==
=== Candidate ===
Former [[University of Montana]] president [[Seth Bodnar]] announced his candidacy as an independent on March 4, 2026, two months after he resigned from the university.<ref name="Campaign Announced">{{cite news |last1=Brown |first1=Matthew |title=Former Montana university leader Seth Bodnar launches independent campaign against GOP Sen. Daines |url=https://apnews.com/article/election-senate-daines-montana-independent-bodnar-3c34598e7d67aadb7cf3dea47bad689a |access-date=5 March 2026 |work=Associated Press |date=4 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Federal Elections Commission |first1=United States |title=Seth Bodnar Filing |url=https://www.fec.gov/data/committee/C00941708/ |website=Seth Bodnar Filing March 4 |publisher=FEC |access-date=29 May 2026}}</ref> He entered the race with the backing of former Democratic senator [[Jon Tester]]. Bodnar submitted 29,964 signatures from 52 of Montana's 56 counties to qualify for the ballot. Of those, 21,284 were accepted, exceeding the required 13,327 signatures.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sosmt.gov/counties-submit-candidate-petition-signatures-to-montana-secretary-of-states-office/|title=Counties submit candidate petition signatures to Montana Secretary of State’s Office - Official Montana Secretary of State Website - Christi Jacobsen}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Drew |first1=Micah |title=Bodnar outraises Alme in pre-primary filings, submits signatures for ballot |url=https://dailymontanan.com/2026/05/26/bodnar-outraises-alme-in-pre-primary-filings-submits-signatures-for-ballot/ |access-date=8 June 2026 |publisher=Daily Montanan |date=26 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Lutey |first1=Tom |title=Former UM president Seth Bodnar enters Montana Senate race as independent |url=https://montanafreepress.org/2026/03/04/bodnar-launches-montana-senate-run/ |access-date=8 June 2026 |publisher=Montana Free Press |date=4 March 2026}}</ref> Paid signature gatherers who worked on behalf of the Bodnar campaign are under investigation by the Cascade County Sheriff's Office.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://montanafreepress.org/2026/09/10/cascade-county-investigating-independent-signatures/|title=Cascade County law enforcement investigating independent candidate signatures|first=Zeke|last=Lloyd|date=September 11, 2026}}</ref> According to the Cascade County Sheriff's Department, the Bodnar campaign is fully cooperating with the investigation and is not itself accused of wrongdoing.

==== Declared ====
*[[Seth Bodnar]], former president of the [[University of Montana]] (2018–2026)<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ambarian |first1=Jonathon |title=Bodnar announces independent run for Senate |url=https://www.kxlh.com/news/bodnar-announces-independent-run-for-senate |access-date=March 4, 2026 |work=[[KXLH]] |date=March 4, 2026}}</ref>

== General election ==
=== Campaign ===
At a June 15 press conference, her first after winning the primary, Bankhead stated she would remain in the race and called upon Bodnar to drop out, citing a gender discrimination lawsuit filed against the University of Montana (UM) in 2021. A spokesperson for the Bodnar campaign said that he had taken claims of discrimination seriously while being president of UM, and that no wrongdoing had been found as a result of the lawsuit.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Thomas |first1=Mariah |title=In Montana Senate Race, Democrat Bankhead Doubles Down on Bid Against Bodnar |url=https://flatheadbeacon.com/2026/06/15/in-montana-senate-race-democrat-bankhead-doubles-down-on-bid-against-bodnar/ |access-date=June 15, 2026 |work=[[Flathead Beacon]] |date=June 15, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260615231703/https://flatheadbeacon.com/2026/06/15/in-montana-senate-race-democrat-bankhead-doubles-down-on-bid-against-bodnar/ |archive-date=June 15, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Bodnar also faced criticism from Montana Republicans, who called him an "independent in name only" and portrayed him as a Democrat seeking to avoid the party label.<ref name="Lutey-independent">{{cite news |last1=Lutey |first1=Tom |title=Bodnar’s big gamble: Why the independent is pushing for Montana’s nonpartisan era |url=https://montanafreepress.org/2026/06/26/how-seth-bodnar-plans-to-become-montana-first-nonpartisan-u-s-senator/ |access-date=August 31, 2026 |work=[[Montana Free Press]] |date=June 26, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Atlantic" /> A Republican-aligned super PAC pointed to Bodnar's registration as a Democrat while he lived in Connecticut in 2012; Montana does not register voters by party.<ref name="Atlantic" /> His advisers said that he would not join either the Democratic or Republican caucus if elected, and Bodnar said he rejected the idea that he would have to submit to a party leader.<ref name="Atlantic" />

As polls show Alme likely to win a three-way race, Democratic leaders increasingly called on their nominee, Bankhead, to drop out of the race, believing Bodnar was their best hope to beat Alme.{{cn|date=August 2026}}

Since mid-July, Montana Freedom PAC, a [[political action committee]] supporting Bodnar, has paid for signs and digital advertising suggesting Bankhead should leave the race. As of early August the committee had spent more than $1 million on advertising benefiting Bodnar.<ref name="Lutey-dropout">{{cite news |last1=Lutey |first1=Tom |title=Scenes from a dropout deadline |url=https://montanafreepress.org/2026/08/06/scenes-from-a-dropout-deadline/ |access-date=August 24, 2026 |work=[[Montana Free Press]] |date=August 6, 2026}}</ref><ref name="fec-mfp">{{cite web |title=Montana Freedom PAC, committee C00943910 |url=https://www.fec.gov/data/committee/C00943910/ |website=fec.gov |publisher=[[Federal Election Commission]] |access-date=August 24, 2026}}</ref>

On the deadline for candidate withdrawal, August 10,<ref name="kpvi" /> ''[[HuffPost]]'' reported that Bankhead was choosing to stay in the race, keeping it a three-way contest.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Blumenthal |first1=Paul |title=Montana Democrat Stays In Senate Race Despite Pressure To Drop Out |url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/montana-senate-2026-bankhead-bodnar_n_6a7a1704e4b0a6d70bb2bf90?origin=article-bottom2-nonlife |access-date=August 10, 2026 |work=The Huffington Post |date=August 10, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>{{bsn|date=August 2026}}

Republicans criticized Bodnar over a transgender athlete's participation in women's sports during his presidency of the University of Montana.<ref name="Brown-2026-Daines">{{cite news |last=Brown |first=Matthew |title=Montana Republican US Sen. Steve Daines drops reelection bid in surprise move |url=https://apnews.com/article/election-senate-daines-montana-independent-bodnar-3c34598e7d67aadb7cf3dea47bad689a |work=Associated Press |date=March 4, 2026 |access-date=September 23, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Scherer-2026-Montana">{{cite news |last=Scherer |first=Michael |title=Big Sky Crack-Up |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/politics/2026/04/montana-democrats-intrigue-bodnar/686852/ |work=The Atlantic |date=April 21, 2026 |access-date=September 23, 2026}}</ref> Asked about the issue at an August campaign event, Bodnar said he favored fairness in women's sports but believed parents and children should make their own decisions.<ref name="Sakariassen-2026-Pulp">{{cite news |last=Sakariassen |first=Alex |title=Bodnar wades into deep red Bitterroot water |url=https://thepulp.org/seth-bodnar-ravalli-county-senate-independent/ |work=The Pulp |date=September 4, 2026 |access-date=September 23, 2026}}</ref> Alme also criticized diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) and accused Bodnar of supporting transgender athletes' participation in girls' sports.<ref name="Sakariassen-2026-Pulp" /><ref name="Plutt-2026-Dillon">{{cite news |last=Plutt |first=J. P. |title=U.S. Senate candidate Alme makes Dillon visit |url=https://www.dillontribune.com/news/u-s-senate-candidate-alme-makes-dillon-visit/article_70282300-2daa-4b1b-a525-4122a3603efc.html |work=Dillon Tribune |date=September 16, 2026 |access-date=September 23, 2026}}</ref>

On October 12, [[Shannon O'Brien (Montana politician)|Shannon O'Brien]], the Chair of the [[Montana Democratic Party|Montana Democratic Party,]] resigned from her position in order to endorse Bodnar's campaign.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Howard |first=Phil |date=2026-10-12 |title=Montana Democratic party chair resigns, endorses Bodnar |url=https://nbcmontana.com/news/local/montana-democratic-party-chair-resigns-endorses-bodnar-10-12-2026 |access-date=2026-10-12 |website=KECI |language=en}}</ref>
